title: For good actions Amyraut adds only the cleansing, strengthening and raising of the faculties
source_text: XXI. Speciatim vero respectu bonarum actionum, praeterea quae jam dicta sunt, non aliud Deo tribuit quam quod facultates ipsas ab adnatis vitiis repurgat, aut novis viribus instruit, & supra nativam ac primigeniam conditionem elevat, quibus actionibus libertatem earum nihil omnino laedi sed adjuvari potius planum est.
pass_a_gloss: XXI. But specially in respect of good actions, besides what has already been said, he attributes nothing else to God than that he purges the faculties themselves from inborn vices, or furnishes them with new strength, and raises them above their native and original condition, by which actions it is plain their freedom is not hurt at all but rather helped.
pass_b_english: With respect to good actions in particular, beyond what has already been said, he ascribes to God only this: that he cleanses the faculties themselves of their inborn faults, or supplies them with new strength and raises them above their native, original condition.
Plainly such acts do not harm the faculties' freedom at all, but rather help it.
